title: Mowing Time Calculator: How Long Will It Take?
description: Estimate mowing time from lawn size, deck width and speed with the Mowing Time Calculator — real-world coverage rates with overlap included. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a one-acre lawn under a 42-inch mower at 3 mph takes about 59 minutes — not the 40 the deck-width brochure implies, because turns and overlap are real.
quick_answer: The Mowing Time Calculator estimates how long a lawn takes from its area, the mower's cutting width and a realistic ground speed, adjusted for overlap and turning efficiency. Enter the lawn size and your mower and read the time — the honest version, not the box's theoretical rate.

Stepping from a 21-inch push mower (about 2½ hours per acre) to a 52-inch zero-turn (about 27 minutes) is a purchase this page prices in the currency that matters: Saturdays.
Crews quote from time. Area, deck and efficiency give the defensible estimate to build a price on — clients accept arithmetic more readily than adjectives.
The bigger yard's hidden cost is mowing hours per season: at 30 cuts a year, the acre at 59 minutes is 30 hours of summer the smaller lot never asks for.

21-inch push mower at 2.5 mph and 75% efficiency: about 151 minutes. 42-inch lawn tractor at 3 mph, 80%: about 59 minutes. 52-inch zero-turn at 5 mph, 85%: about 27 minutes. Deck width and speed are both levers; efficiency is the tax collector.

Passes overlap a few inches, turns cost seconds, and obstacles tax every lap. Golf-course fairway units with wide decks and no trees approach 85–90%; a fenced yard with a trampoline lives nearer 65–75%.

popular_table.title: Coverage rates that survive contact with lawns
popular_table.note: Rates assume grass that is being maintained, not rescued. First cuts of the season, wet grass and bagging all slow the real pace — the efficiency slider is where honesty enters.

faq: Open, rectangular, obstacle-free lawns: 80–85%. Typical suburban yards with beds, trees and fences: 70–80%. Obstacle obstacle-courses with a push mower: 60–70%. When in doubt, 75% is the grizzled default.
Bagging or mulching — does it matter?
Bagging adds emptying stops (5–10% slower in leaf season and spring flush); mulching and side-discharge run clean. The efficiency input is where the difference belongs.
Slopes cut ground speed and raise caution, especially with tractors. Drop the speed a notch for hilly ground rather than discovering the adjustment mid-slope.
How do I get my lawn's mowable area?
House, drive, beds and woods do not get mowed. Measure the grass polygons in the Map Area Calculator, or subtract the obvious non-lawn from the lot size.
A show lawn cut twice takes twice as long — run the calculator twice mentally or halve the effective width. Cross-hatching is a labour of love, priced accordingly.
Time per visit × visits per season × your hourly rate is the skeleton; travel, trimming and edging add on. This calculator owns the mowing line of that quote — trimming a big yard can rival it.
They invert the problem: coverage is about battery cycles and weeks, not a single session. The per-acre rates here explain why the robot needs all week — it is a 20-inch deck with infinite patience.
